newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares recover after soft open, await cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares recover after soft open, await cabinet.

text.p: Greek equities recovered after a weak open to close with mild gains on strong turnover of 10.7 billion drachmas with attention focused on the new socialist cabinet expected to be announced Wednesday, analysts said.

"If the market stays saggy it will prompt additional selling in the short term and the only way this will be offset is by inflows by foreign funds. Any weakness ahead should be seen as a buying opportunity in selective areas," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.

From a sectoral viewpoint, bank shares, plastics and cosmetics had favourable prospects. Also liked were shares of high tech printer Inform Lykos, National Insurance and cosmetics firm Papaellinas, he said.

"PASOK, the party that was given the mandate to govern for the next four years is clearly more conservative than the PASOK we knew before the passing of Andreas Papandreou. Hence, the collective wish of the people points to a willingness to accept economic austerity," Varsos said.

Prime Minister Costas Simitis received a mandate from the president of the republic to form a new four-year government on Monday. With 99.5 percent of the vote counted, the socialists have a comfortable 162-seat majority in the 300-seat parliament.

On Monday, brokers had trouble explaining the retreat of the benchmark index but some suggested that there was concerted selling by some local growth funds and speculators who rushed to close out long positions once the market lost steam.
There was also position squaring in construction stocks and investors showed a cautious stance before the government unveils its economic policy.
The Athens general share index closed 0.46 percent, or 4.45 points higher at 962.86, the session's high from Monday's 958.41 close after opening at 958.41 points.
Turnover rose to 10.77 billion drachmas from 9.92 billion on Monday on volume of 6.34 million shares. It was boosted by block trades in Michaniki and Aspis Pronia.
Bourse newcomer, small-cap Vernicos Yaughts climbed 8.0 percent in its trade debut to close at 1,620 drachmas. It went public at 1,500 drachnmas.

Losers led gainers by 105 to 101 with 32 issues unchanged on 238 traded. Banks gained 0.19 percent, industrials edged 0.33 percent higher and construction firmed 0.52 percent. Small-caps put on gains of 0.19 percent.
